title: Why the Sky Turns Red at Sunset
summary: A 4-scene vertical explainer on why sunsets look red, using a vivid but accurate analogy about light being filtered through a longer path in air.

scenes.title: Why red at sunset?
scenes.narration: Why does the sky suddenly glow red at sunset? It’s not the Sun changing color. It’s sunlight taking a much longer trip through the air.

scenes.title: Blue gets scattered first
scenes.narration: Think of the atmosphere like a giant sifter. Shorter blue wavelengths get tossed around in every direction, while red light slips through more easily.

scenes.title: Noon versus sunset
scenes.narration: At noon, sunlight passes through less air, so plenty of blue is scattered across the whole sky. At sunset, that extra filtering leaves warmer colors behind.

scenes.title: The sunset takeaway
scenes.narration: So a red sunset is really the atmosphere sorting sunlight by color. Longer path, more scattering, redder sky.
